security_review.dcc_review:
DCC SECURITY REVIEW - 2026-11-15 America/Los_Angeles
Baseline: onekeyirc 0.1.24; candidate tree: onekeyirc 0.1.25.

Reviewed src/dcc.c, dcc.h, dcc_commands.c, dcc_commands.h, the incoming
CTCP boundary in app.c/idle.c, and existing DCC/identity regressions.

CONFIRMED AND FIXED

Severity assessment: moderate availability/resource-consumption defect,
conditioned on an explicitly accepted active DCC transfer.

A user-accepted DCC receiver retained POLLIN while an ACK was pending.
receive_step flushes the ACK before it will consume additional payload. If
the peer stops consuming ACKs while incoming payload is readable, poll wakes
immediately on input and receive_step returns EAGAIN on the blocked ACK.
This repeats without progress. Unsolicited offers alone cannot trigger it:
a live transfer requires explicit user acceptance. The idle timeout can
terminate a transfer that makes no progress for 120 seconds.

The fix is a one-line readiness-policy change in src/dcc.c plus explanatory
comments: pending ACKs (including partial writes and empty-file ACK0) select
POLLOUT only. After the ACK flushes, normal POLLIN interest resumes.

The new real-loopback regression fills the actual TCP ACK send buffer with
ACK-shaped bytes and leaves four payload bytes unread. There are no mocked
send, recv or poll calls. The original source produces 256 readiness wakes
without progress in 256 iterations; fixed source produces zero. The fixture
then drains the peer, resumes the transfer and verifies exact final bytes.
It includes production dcc.c so it can obtain the active transfer's socket
for buffer setup; this is a focused transport fixture, not a complete CLI
DCC session test. The full existing DCC unit suite also passes.

VALIDATION

Strict C11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror builds passed.
Baseline new regression: expected exit 1 (confirmed failure).
Fixed new regression: exit 0, normal and ASan/UBSan.
Existing DCC suite: exit 0, normal and ASan/UBSan.
Existing source-identity replacement regression: exit 0.
Sanitizers use detect_leaks=0; no leak-check pass is claimed.
Exact commands, output, durations and executable hashes: dcc-results.json.

OTHER SECURITY RESULTS

No additional concrete defect found in strict decimal/size/name parsing,
Unicode/control refusal, bounded offers (8) and active transfers (4),
offline guards, explicit accept/send, descriptor-relative path walking,
symlink refusal, source inode identity, exclusive 0600 receive creation,
owned private final receive directories, no-overwrite behavior, cancellation
cleanup, stale descriptor/id snapshots, byte-count limits, ACK validation,
or offer/transfer timeouts.

Classic DCC remains an explicit, unencrypted and unauthenticated peer
transfer. Its listening sender accepts the first TCP peer; the offered IRC
nickname is not cryptographic proof of that TCP peer's identity. This is a
pre-existing protocol/design limit, not changed by this patch. No automatic
DCC connection or file write occurs merely on receiving an offer.

EFFICIENCY/STABILITY NOTES FOR LATER PHASES

Duplicate valid ACKs currently set the display-progress flag even when the
acknowledged byte count does not advance. Redraw reporting is throttled to
100 ms and duplicates do not renew the transfer idle timeout, so this is a
small optional efficiency opportunity, not another confirmed security bug.
File I/O uses selected regular files synchronously; a slow filesystem can
still delay the single event loop during an explicitly active transfer.
No asynchronous storage redesign was attempted in this security pass.

CHANGED FILES

src/dcc.c
tests/test_dcc_backpressure.c

The new test includes dcc.c directly. Build it with:
  cc ... -Isrc tests/test_dcc_backpressure.c src/protocol.c -o TEST_BINARY
Do not additionally link src/dcc.c. Parent owns Makefile/docs/version edits.

FOLLOW-UP EFFICIENCY/STABILITY REVIEW

Remote EOF/error paths terminate the specific transfer, close its socket
and file descriptors, and unlink an incomplete receive file only when the
stable directory-relative inode still matches the file originally created.
A renamed/replaced path is preserved. Outgoing source files are never
unlinked. Existing regressions exercise short receive/EOF, oversize payload,
partial cancellation, replacement preservation, source truncation, timeout,
fragmented/invalid acknowledgements and zero-length completion.

Each active transfer gets its own iteration in dcc_process, with at most
four data batches (16 KiB each) and sixteen ACK reads per invocation. Stable
transfer IDs plus descriptor matching reject stale poll snapshots. A blocked
or completed transfer does not skip later active slots. Regular-file I/O
remains synchronous; the caps are work bounds, not wall-clock disk latency
bounds. No additional concrete disconnect, cancellation, or independent-
transfer fairness defect was found. No speculative refactor or extra test
was added for these already-covered paths.

Without a configured server, startup opens a disconnected workspace with
only vipirc in the header. Open Settings to add a server, or supply --server.
In an interactive full-interface launch, an unconfigured nickname on the
selected primary connection is requested with your system login as the
default. Enter accepts it; typed text replaces it. Saved secondary profiles
and unattended startup use the existing valid login default, or user when
the login name is unsuitable. An explicit --nick takes precedence.
The server can reject a nickname under its own rules.

If no channel is selected, the initial conversation is the server view,
including the server's welcome messages and message of the day (MOTD).
Configured channels are joined after successful registration and required
authentication. The server can refuse a channel join. Open Servers through
F2 or /servers to manage connections. It supports up to
eight sessions, each with its own channels, queries, and settings.

The client starts ready to type with a visible caret. Enter sends to the
current channel or query after the usual message checks. Server and mentions
views have no implicit chat recipient. Open Command through the vipirc panel,
or type / at chat caret position zero, to use /join or /msg. Tab completes
nicknames and Shift-Tab cycles matches backwards. F1 opens vipirc, F2
Servers, F3 Channels, F4 Queries, F5 Mentions/unread, and F6 File
transfers. Each opens an available panel immediately. Escape from a query
opens Queries; Escape from other chat views opens vipirc. Escape from an
ordinary panel returns to chat. Settings returns to vipirc on Escape. Arrow
keys stay in the editor or panel body.

The full interface keeps the terminal's foreground and background colors,
including empty screen areas. Focus uses bold printable outlines, without
forcing white or black or changing the terminal's color palette. The same
emphasis works on monochrome terminals.

For a literal message beginning with /, type // followed by the rest of the
message. Bracketed pasted text is always treated as text, even when it
begins with /. Pasting does not send the text automatically.

GETTING HELP

    vipirc -h              command-line summary; --help is equivalent
    vipirc -v              program version; --version is equivalent
    vipirc --manual        this complete manual on standard output
    man vipirc             installed system manual page
    /help or /manual       Open the complete manual inside the client
    /help TEXT             Search the manual for TEXT

Press ? while navigating to explain both the selected item and its screen.
For example, selecting Settings on the vipirc main screen opens help headed
"Settings is an option on the vipirc main screen." The help browser includes
an About screen link and the selected item's instructions. Left/Right or
Tab chooses a help action, and Enter follows it; the mouse can activate it
too. Escape from screen help returns to item help; Escape again restores
the originating screen, selection, scroll position, and unfinished input.
If nothing is selected, help explains the screen. In an editable text field,
including an empty field, ? remains ordinary text. In Command, select a
suggestion with Down before pressing ? for its help.

The vipirc header destination opens an application panel. The welcome
warning appears beneath vipirc | ThatIAm.vip, before Server, Nick, and the
connection summary. A blank line precedes Settings, Manual, Command, and
Background; another blank line precedes About and Insha-Allah license
agreement. Select a choice with Up/Down or k/j and
Enter. Server and Nick open the current profile's settings; Nick selects its
nickname field. Disconnected diagnostics show applied connection choices;
connected diagnostics describe the current live session. Insha-Allah license
agreement opens the complete included license, also offline; Escape, Enter,
q, or Back returns from the license reader to vipirc.

About shows the program version, ThatIAm.vip website, designer remfan1994,
and license name. It also displays an on-demand local snapshot: process ID,
session uptime, accumulated user/system CPU time, peak resident memory
where the units are supported, and server/channel/query counts. Peak
resident memory is a maximum, not current memory consumption; CPU totals
are not a live percentage. Unsupported values are marked unavailable.
No background resource sampler is used. Escape, Enter, q, or Back returns
from About to vipirc.

/help, /manual, and /view help open the complete manual directly. It works
disconnected and preserves the underlying chat view, draft, and caret.
In the full interface, /help TEXT searches within that manual; it does not
print a separate topic explanation. Text may be a phrase or command name.
The reader contains documentation without a live Server/Connection/Nick
diagnostics block, chat field, or Input/Navigation label. Up/Down or k/j
scrolls a line, Page Up/Page Down scrolls a page, and Home/End or g/G reaches
the beginning/end. A manual opened from the vipirc application screen
shows Return to: vipirc and returns there. A direct /manual or /help returns
to its prior chat. Escape, q, and Back follow that origin when search entry
is not active.

The toolbar beneath the Manual heading contains Back, Search, Previous,
and Next. Back is selected initially. Left/Right or h/l selects a toolbar
action; Enter executes it. The return destination is displayed below the
toolbar and documentation follows.

Press / or activate Search to enter a literal UTF-8 search string of up
to 256 bytes. Enter finds a match; Escape cancels search entry and stays
in the reader. While reading, n or Next finds the next match; N or Previous
finds the previous one. Search wraps at either end of the manual and ignores
ASCII letter case; other characters match literally. This is not a regular
expression or an IRC command. Search remains local and is not added to
command history. Pasted text is ignored in both the reader and search entry.
View cycling skips the manual. F1 through F6
open other available application categories directly.

MINIMALIST INTERFACE

    vipirc -i
    vipirc --idle --test-mode
    vipirc -i --manual

-i/--idle selects the command-oriented interface while using the same
vipirc configurations and server catalog. After the welcome:

    /connect irc.ircnow.org
    /join #ircnow
    /saveconf

The nickname defaults to your valid system login name, or user as a fallback.
Use /nick NICK to change it. /saveconf saves preferences and healthy server
profiles and makes the selected connection the default for a later launch,
including a selected secondary server. /connect alone then reuses that
saved choice. Saving does not enable auto-connect. The guided /quickstart and
/panel screens are optional.

For normal startup in either interface, --nick, --port, --channel, --tls, --plain and
--ca-file apply to the remembered default connection. An explicit --server
selects the primary connection and takes precedence over that remembered
choice. If the default is unavailable, non-host overrides fail with an
instruction to supply --server or repair the default. --init-config and
--check-config apply their overrides to the primary configuration.

The native syntax is /connect [-tls|-plain] [-nick NICK] HOST [PORT]. New
servers
use verified TLS on port 6697. -plain explicitly selects unencrypted IRC
and defaults to 6667. A bare port does not disable TLS; +PORT selects TLS.
-ssl is a supported -tls alias. /server HOST uses the same direct route.
A matching saved server retains its transport, port, nickname, and auth
settings; a new destination starts with fresh credentials. /query NICK|NUMBER
opens a private conversation, and /pm NICK|NUMBER remains an alias.

In its log view, / opens a command editor. Another ordinary key opens the
composer and retains the character; Enter opens an empty field. Line mode
is the default: one input row stays below a live retained tail. Fullscreen
keeps a multi-line editor while reserving a smaller live-tail pane. Incoming
IRC activity repaints that tail without moving the draft caret. Escape cancels an
editor or pending review, including when no send target has been selected;
Escape in the log backgrounds the client. Ctrl-C terminates,
Ctrl-Z suspends, fg resumes, and Ctrl-D is inert. /background keeps the
client running after detaching; suspension pauses networking.

The default [input] send_mode=direct sends on Enter. send_mode=review opens
a temporary alternate-screen review; the draft and Send prompt do not become
chat transcript lines. A fresh Enter confirms, typing returns to editing, and
Escape cancels. Reaching the computed one-message byte budget requires
Enter acknowledgement before more text can be added. Splitting across several
IRC lines still requires separate send-time approval. Recognized bracketed paste never executes
commands or sends automatically. Tab completes commands or nicknames.
Down selects a command suggestion and Enter inserts it for editing; a
separate Enter after the input is displayed executes it. Up from the command
input recalls accepted commands. Log and full-text command history are
bounded in RAM; canonical command names and usage counts have a separate
private .commands file, described under COMMAND PROMPT.

/help ls lists help topics. /help commands explains command use and lists
commands. /help autoconnect, /help autojoin, /help autoauth, and /help away
give focused instructions. /manual, vipirc -i --manual, and the separate
doc/vipirc-idle-manual.txt provide the complete minimalist reference. Its
commands and controls differ from the curses interface documented below.

/quickstart optionally guides the current server's server, TLS transport,
port, and nickname settings. /panel takes no arguments and opens the Panel
selector. Its default choice is 0 Application preferences. That path edits
History lines, Send mode, Composer mode, Output format, Queue notices, Program
messages, Persistent logging, Single-session mode, Command suggestions, and
Default interface. That preference selects the next fresh launch without
switching the current frontend. The panel then offers 1 Save (default)
or 2 Apply without saving. It works before configuring a server and never
connects or switches the selected chat. These global preferences remain in
the main configuration file.

Server panels 1 through 8 edit connection, startup, authentication, watch,
and ignore settings. They omit the application-wide preferences. Their
final choices are 1 Save and connect, 2 Save only (default), 3 Connect once,
and 4 Apply only. Quickstart uses the same final choices but defaults to 3.
Enter keeps a shown value; '-' clears optional fields. Escape returns to the
previous question. At the Panel selector or first
Quickstart question it closes setup and discards unapplied edits. Tab selects
the question heading; ? there opens help for that question and its screen.
Tab or Enter returns to answer editing, where ? always remains literal.
Plaintext password
input is hidden, answers never enter command history, and credential files
are not read while editing.

Opening setup and answering earlier questions does not apply, save, or
connect. Connect once applies without saving; Apply only neither saves nor
connects. Existing connections are never implicitly retargeted or reconnected.
A failed connection does not undo changes already applied or saved by the
explicit final action. The question-by-question /panel and /quickstart flows
are shared by both
interfaces. Graphical /settings and F1 Settings retain the ordinary forms.

Native server numbers start at 1 throughout /servers, /server NUMBER,
/connect NUMBER, and server labels such as S1. Server 1 is the permanent
primary server. Choice 0 in Panel means application preferences, not a
server. Channel 0 still shows the selected server's messages and MOTD.
The full interface keeps server numbers from 0. Saved profile identities
and the configuration layout are unchanged.

Ordinary selected-chat output defaults to [HH:MM:SS] <nickname> text.
/set output_format full includes date, server, and target metadata;
/set output_format compact restores the concise form. /save output saves
this global choice in the main config file as [output] format=compact|full.
Aggregate mentions retain the origin needed to identify their conversation.

Help, /manual, and multiline command results use a separate reader with
ASCII headings and dividers. They are not inserted into chat history.
Up/Down, Page Up/Page Down, and Home/End navigate the response; Escape
returns to chat. Enter scrolls help. A successful /users or /users #channel
roster instead closes with Enter, Escape, or q and restores the previously
selected chat log, including when the roster is empty. Arrow and page keys
still browse long rosters. Incoming chat remains bounded in RAM and networking
continues while reading. A slash opens Command from the reader; Escape
before executing the command restores the reader. Executing a new command
replaces the previous response. Short acknowledgments remain
ordinary notices. --manual still prints plain text for shell use.
Normal native screens omit recurring key hints. /help keys retains the
complete keyboard reference. Command usage, real errors, byte counts, and
send warnings remain visible when relevant.

The primary profile's [input] send_mode and composer_mode apply globally in idle mode.
Use /set send_mode direct|review, /set composer_mode line|fullscreen, and
/save input to persist those choices. Line mode is the default.
This field is retained when the full interface saves a profile.
Idle mode uses the primary history limit across all conversations; the
full interface continues to use per-conversation history limits. The
minimalist interface has optional persistent transcript logging, off by
default, and no graphical DCC forms. It supports the same explicit active IPv4
DCC SEND operations through /dcc commands, without a curses display dependency.

COMMAND-LINE OPTIONS

    -i, --idle
        Open the minimalist command-oriented interface with the normal
        vipirc configuration. --manual and --help then describe that mode.
        Override the saved default for this invocation without saving it.

    -N, --ncurses
        Open the full ncurses interface for this invocation, overriding the
        saved default without changing it. If both -i and -N occur, the last
        explicit interface option wins. Lowercase -n still takes a nickname.

    --resume [JOB]
        See also --background below for unattended startup in either mode.
        Resume the sole verified available detached vipirc job, or select its
        number with --resume JOB or --resume=JOB. vipirc --resume retains that
        live session's frontend; vipirc -N --resume selects ncurses and
        vipirc -i --resume selects the minimalist frontend. Multiple candidates are listed and
        require a number. An unverified candidate also prevents automatic
        selection. Requires an interactive terminal. An explicit absolute
        socket path is still accepted for older sessions.
    --sessions
        List this account's attached and detached local vipirc jobs without loading
        configuration or requiring a terminal. These management operations
        are separate: do not combine them with one another or with connection
        and configuration options, which belong to a new process.
    --detach-session NUMBER
        Non-destructively release the terminal/controller from the verified
        numbered job while keeping its IRC worker, connections, drafts,
        transfers and retained history alive. After success, attach the new
        terminal with --resume NUMBER. This is the recovery command for an
        old SSH terminal that is gone while --sessions still says attached.
        Run it as the account that owns the job.
    --close-session NUMBER
        Close the whole local vipirc job identified by its current number
        in --sessions; this is not a process ID. All IRC connections and
        transfers in the job end, and unsaved drafts and in-memory history
        are discarded. Configuration files remain. --close-session=NUMBER
        is also accepted. No terminal or configuration load is required.
        Success requires verified application teardown and release of the
        original job lease, not just request acceptance. Older or
        unresponsive workers may refuse or time out. An accepted request
        may still finish after a timeout; recheck --sessions. See CLOSE A
        SESSION FROM THE SHELL for details.

    --background
        Start directly as a detached job without an interactive terminal.
        Uses the saved default interface, or ncurses if unset; add -i for
        minimalist mode or -N for ncurses for this launch. A later bare
        --resume retains the worker's current frontend.
        Prints the usual warning without waiting for a key. A missing nick
        uses the valid system login name, or user if that name is unsuitable.
        Use saved autoconnect profiles or --server; --no-connect wins.
        Success means the local job is ready, not that IRC login succeeded.
    --reconnect
        Retry transient connection failures for this process. Does not
        initiate connections or change saved autoconnect preferences.
        Delays are 5, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, then 300 seconds maximum.
        Sixty seconds of registration resets backoff. /disconnect cancels
        pending retry; /connect restarts explicitly. TLS verification,
        authentication, protocol and configuration failures remain held.
        Pending messages are discarded, not resent. Authentication, saved
        autojoin and enabled startup-command lists run on each connection.
        Staged connection settings still require an explicit /connect.

    -s, --server HOST
        Select a server hostname or numeric IPv4/IPv6 address. Supply a host,
        not an irc:// URL. Use --port for the port.
    -p, --port PORT
        Select a TCP port in the range 1 through 65535.
    -c, --channel CHANNEL
        Auto-join a channel after registration. A comma-separated list or
        repeated --channel options selects several channels.
    -n, --nick NICK
        Select a nickname on the effective startup profile. First-use
        interactive primary startup can prompt with your system login as
        the default; unattended startup uses a valid default without asking.
    -C, --config FILE
        Select the primary server configuration and its adjacent server
        catalog. Without --server, connection overrides apply to the
        remembered default server. An explicit --server selects the primary
        profile; --init-config and --check-config also use it. The default is
        $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/vipirc/config.ini when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set, or
        $HOME/.config/vipirc/config.ini otherwise. XDG_CONFIG_HOME must be
        absolute. An explicitly selected file must exist except when it is
        being created with --init-config.
    --tls
        Use verified TLS. The usual default TLS port is 6697.
    --plain
        Explicitly select unencrypted IRC. The usual default plain port is
        6667. Automatic authentication is refused with this transport.
    --ca-file FILE
        Use an explicit PEM certificate authority file for TLS verification.
        Its authorities are trusted in place of the system default store.
    --no-connect
        Start all server sessions without connecting. In test mode, leave
        all simulators stopped. Use /connect for the current server, or
        Connect in the Servers list, when ready.
    --test-mode
        Load normal settings and run interactive, bounded IRC simulation
        inside this process. No network sockets, DNS, credential-file reads,
        or GPG
        are used.
        Missing server/nickname values do not prompt. See OFFLINE TEST MODE.
    --init-config
        Create a configuration file and exit. Existing files are not
        overwritten. Combine with --server, --channel, and --nick to write
        initial connection values.
    --check-config
        Validate the primary configuration, command-line values, adjacent
        server catalog, and referenced profiles, then exit. This does not
        test server reachability or prove credentials work.
    --manual
        Write the complete manual to standard output and exit.
    -h, --help
        Write command-line help and exit.
    -v, --version
        Write the program version and exit.
    -V
        Compatibility alias for --version.

Long options accept --name=value. Short options accept the normal combined
option syntax. -- ends option parsing; positional arguments are not used.
Command-line values override the selected configuration, which overrides
built-in defaults. Explicit --port is available when a network uses a
different port from the transport's usual default.
Selecting a different --server clears inherited account/server-password
settings and inherited auto-join channels; specify channels for that server.
Additional servers have separate saved profiles. A different --config path
selects a different primary configuration and workspace catalog.

-h, -v, --manual, and --check-config exit without an interactive terminal
or welcome screen. --test-mode cannot be combined with --init-config or
--check-config; either combination is a usage error (exit status 2).

OFFLINE TEST MODE

    vipirc --test-mode
    vipirc --test-mode --config /absolute/config.ini
    vipirc --test-mode --no-connect

The simulator loads the selected configuration and runs the actual
interface, input editor, filters, and applicable protocol/queue handling.
It produces bounded synthetic IRC activity and membership changes. It
opens no network socket, performs no DNS lookup, and reads no password or
CA file. Configured servers are display labels; nothing is sent there.
The primary and saved secondary profiles each run separate simulations.
Servers > New adds more simulated sessions, without changing this mode.

After the welcome screen is dismissed, simulation starts even when the
configuration has autoconnect=false. --no-connect leaves all simulators
stopped until explicitly connected. /disconnect stops the current simulator;
/connect starts only that session's simulation. To connect to a real server,
exit and relaunch without --test-mode.

Missing server and nickname values do not cause prompts. The nickname uses
the system login name when valid, or a test nickname otherwise. Configured
channels are used; if none are selected, #test-one and #test-two are supplied.
Server/MOTD remains channel 0. The client starts ready to type. Escape
opens Queries from a query or vipirc from other chat views. F1 through F6
open available category panels. Escape from an ordinary panel returns to
chat; Settings returns to vipirc.
The vipirc panel provides Settings and Command. /channels and /ql also
open the lists; /pm NICK|NUMBER opens a query.

Try fixed-height input, Backspace across rows, resize, paste, the immediate
message-limit warning, and multi-message send confirmation. Inspect
mentions and user lists while simulated events arrive. The same
retained-history bounds and applicable message queue and pacing rules apply.
The local simulator is part of the C client and does not require Python
or an external IRC daemon.

The scheduled event interval is two seconds. A cycle includes channel text,
a nickname mention, a configured custom watch string, a private message,
and a participant joining, changing nickname, receiving voice, and leaving.
All current custom watch strings are tried in rotation, one string per
16-second activity cycle. /watch changes affect the next watch event.
For a stable list of k strings, the sequence repeats every 16*k seconds.
If no custom watch string is configured, the demo gives a /watch example.
/msg NICK TEXT produces a labelled simulated private reply. Channel text
is locally echoed. JOIN, PART, NICK, WHOIS, TOPIC, and AWAY receive simulated
responses; the simulator does not implement every IRC server behavior or
enforce keyed-channel access.

File transfers displays a memory-only sample offer. You can review, reject,
or cancel it; Send and Accept are disabled before any file or socket access.
Closing a secondary test server removes only its runtime row, leaving saved
catalog and profile files unchanged.

/save is disabled in test mode. Interface changes remain in memory and
cannot overwrite real connection settings through that command. To try a
permanent configuration edit, edit the file with your text editor and
restart. This mode does not create or modify a config file automatically.

--check-config is a separate noninteractive syntax/value check. It reads
the primary configuration, catalog, and referenced profiles, reports the
result, and exits. --test-mode
adds interactive inspection of simulated behavior. Neither validates a
real hostname's reachability, TLS certificate, SASL identity, password,
authentication-service behavior, or actual delivery to IRC users.

GLOBAL HEADER AND CHAT CONTROLS

The client starts in chat editing. The header contains categories with
content, always in this relative order:

    F1 vipirc                 application controls, settings, help, About,
    license
    F2 Servers (N)            configured or retained server sessions
    F3 Channels (N)           this server's retained channel views
    F4 Queries (N)            this server's separate private conversations
    F5 Mentions/unread (M/U)   timestamped mentions and unread source
    conversations
    F6 File transfers (N)     retained transfers across all servers

vipirc is always present. A fresh workspace without a server shows only
vipirc. Empty lists take no header space. A parted channel with retained
history and a completed transfer record still count as content.
Mentions/unread
is available while any server has retained mention lines or unread source
conversations. M counts the retained mention lines; U counts unread source
conversations. Reading a mention does not remove its retained line. Counts
appear in parentheses after the label, separately from the shortcut number;
for example, F2 Servers (2) and F3 Channels (12).

Visible categories are separated by ' > '. Each keeps its function key F1
through F6 even when earlier empty categories are hidden. A function key
opens its available category immediately; hidden categories are not created
by a shortcut. Function keys are decoded using the terminal's TERM entry.
Plain digits in chat remain ordinary text. Pasted escape sequences never
invoke these shortcuts.
If the terminal reserves a function key for its own action, adjust that
terminal binding so the key reaches the client.

Settings > Interface > Shortcut labels controls the F1..F6 prefixes, which
are shown by default. Turning it off leaves the names, counts and separators
visible, and all six function keys keep their fixed roles. Apply changes
every server session; Save writes [interface] shortcut_labels=false or true
in the primary configuration. This setting is independent of Hints.

A solid divider separates the top bar from the screen below.
The current conversation has its own row below that divider. A query nickname
never replaces Queries. Narrow terminals scroll the header to keep the
selected available category reachable.

F1..F6 immediately open the available panel's body. Arrow keys operate
the editor, list, or actions; they never focus or cycle the top bar. Up at
the first input row stays in the editor. Escape in a query opens Queries
with that query selected, regardless of its entry route. Escape in other
chat views opens vipirc; F1 always opens vipirc directly. Escape from an
ordinary panel restores the previous chat draft and caret. Escape from
Settings returns to vipirc, and the IALA
reader also returns there. Safety dialogs and captured paste keep their own
handling first. A practical setup route is F1 to configure a server,
F2 to connect or read server messages, F3 to join or select channels, and
F4 for private queries.

On the F1 vipirc panel, Escape asks Really quit? [Y/N]. Only a fresh y or Y
confirms. Any other ordinary key cancels and stays on vipirc. Pasted input,
mouse clicks, and resize events cannot confirm. Use b or Back (b) on vipirc
to return to chat. Ctrl-C and Ctrl-Z keep their normal terminal signal roles.

In chat, arrows move the caret, Home/End reaches draft endpoints, and hjkl
and other letters are literal text. Page Up/Page Down scroll the history.
In the minimalist -i main chat view, Up scrolls one retained row older,
Page Up scrolls a page, and Home jumps to the oldest retained page. Down,
Page Down and End stay or return to the live tail. Left, Right, Delete and
Backspace are inert there. Insert or Enter opens an empty composer. Escape
backgrounds from the live log and returns from the scrollback reader.
Tab completes a nickname; Shift-Tab cycles matching names backwards. A typed
slash at caret position zero opens the separate Command prompt.

Selected item text and brackets use bold emphasis without dim hint styling.
The complete chat-field border marks editing focus on the terminal's normal
colors.
Monochrome terminals retain bold text and visible brackets. No
Input/Navigation status label or appearance selector is
needed; legacy focus_style entries are accepted only for migration.

Clear and Send sit below the fixed field only when mouse reporting is
available and enabled. Enter sends and /clearinput clears the full draft,
including offscreen text, with or without a mouse. Sending always follows
the same validation, byte warning, and default-No multi-message review.
Send-queue feedback uses the separate status area.

Server/channel/query list actions appear directly below the heading and
above the items. Up/Down or k/j selects an item and Left/Right or h/l
chooses its action. Enter executes that action;
Open is selected initially. The item and action are highlighted together.
Changing the item preserves the action, and Up/Down stops at the first/last
item. Horizontal arrows stay in the list; A function key or a header click
opens
another available category.
Delete invokes Close for the selected server, channel, or query with the
same confirmation and protected-entry rules as the action row. Server 0
cannot be closed. Inside editors Delete still removes text under the caret.
The channel list always includes server/MOTD as entry 0. Empty Queries can
still be reached with /ql and includes New query...; Join/New opens Command
with /join or /pm prepared. Slash commands also open empty categories that
are absent from the header.

Main chat paste stays literal, including a leading slash, and never sends
automatically. Pasted tabs become spaces. Lists, readers, category navigation,
and safety dialogs ignore bracketed paste. Command and active Settings or
transfer editors accept data according to their sections.

NICKNAME COMPLETION

Tab completes the nickname token at the chat caret. Further Tab presses
cycle matching names in case-aware alphabetical order, wrapping; Shift-Tab
cycles backwards. Matching follows this server's advertised ASCII, strict
RFC1459, or RFC1459 nickname case rules. No lookup or outgoing message is
needed. Ordinary editing ends the current completion cycle.

At the beginning of a draft, completion adds ': '. At the end of a later
word it adds a space. Existing punctuation and following words remain
intact when completing inside a draft. Channels and URLs are not interpreted
as nickname prefixes. A candidate that would exceed the draft's byte or
character bound leaves the entire draft intact. Crossing the smaller IRC
message budget opens the normal early warning; completion never sends.

A channel uses its current roster. A query uses its peer and your nickname.
Server and mention views use peers known from this server's joined channels
and query list. Another server's users are never candidates. Current roster
changes apply to the next completion, without storing an extra user list.

COMMAND PROMPT

Select Command or press / in the F1 vipirc application panel to open it
from any chat caret position. Typing / at chat caret position zero also opens
it, even
when a chat draft already exists. The original chat text
and exact caret position remain intact. A slash elsewhere in chat is ordinary
text. Pasted slashes always remain literal chat text.

The prompt has its own editor, suggestions, and Run/Cancel controls. Settings
> Interface > Command suggestions selects one of five modes:

    Commonly used: the default curated order of useful commands, adapted to
      connection and conversation state. This is not measured popularity.
    Recent history: accepted command lines from this server session, newest
      first, with their original arguments.
    Most used with this configuration: commands ranked by personal usage
      counts associated with this server's configuration.
    Alphabetical: implemented command names in alphabetical order.
    Contextual: commands ranked for the screen that opened Command. Channel
      origins prioritize /me and /topic; server origins prioritize /join and
      /list; query origins prioritize /me and /whois; client screens such as
      vipirc and Summary prioritize /summary, /servers, /settings and /quit.

Contextual captures the actual opener, even if a channel remains selected
under another screen. Ranking keeps matching commands from other categories
available. Type a name prefix to narrow the list; names match ASCII without
case sensitivity. Argument values are not predicted.

Down highlights a suggestion. Up/Down then moves through suggestions; Up
from the first one returns to the input. Enter inserts the selected command
without executing it. Existing arguments remain intact for a catalog row;
a history row inserts its complete retained line. Review or edit the result,
then press Enter again after it has been displayed. Extra Enter keys in the
same pending input batch cannot turn insertion into execution. ? on a
highlighted suggestion opens command help with a link to Command screen help.
Closing help restores the input and selection. A typed ? in the input is
ordinary text.

Delete on a Recent history row removes that stored line. Delete on a Most
used row resets its personal usage count. The command itself remains
available. Catalog suggestions cannot be deleted. Outside a selected
suggestion, Delete edits the input normally.

Suggestions use available rows, with their range and total. Page Up/Page
Down and the mouse wheel browse them. A terminal too small to show a
suggestion cannot select one invisibly. Right at the end of a command-name
prefix completes it; repeated Right cycles matches. Clicking a candidate
also inserts it. Tab does not navigate the header or execute a command.
Nickname completion remains in the chat field.

Up from the input recalls progressively older accepted commands matching
the original typed prefix. While browsing that history, Down returns toward
newer entries and restores the original line. Argument prefixes match
byte-for-byte. Failed commands remain editable and are not recorded.

History is bounded to 64 entries and 64 KiB of strings including terminators.
Consecutive identical entries are not duplicated; oldest entries are evicted
at either bound. UTF-8 arguments are preserved exactly. No command history is
written to configuration files or disk, and it ends with that server session.

Usage counts are separate from those complete history lines. The sole
persistent count file is <config_path>.commands beside each authoritative
server configuration. It stores at most 96 canonical command names and
bounded counts, with no arguments, channel names, messages, or passwords.
Automatic count-file reads and writes require a saved configuration. Until
the first successful Save, an unsaved profile keeps its counts in memory.
Normal accepted commands and frequency resets then update the file using
private atomic replacement. The main configuration does not store counts.
Test mode neither reads nor writes these count files. Missing or unusable
count files do not prevent startup. Full-text history stays in RAM.

Keyed /join commands are omitted entirely. Messages to common services such
as NickServ/AuthServ/ChanServ, and messages beginning authentication verbs
such as IDENTIFY, AUTH, LOGIN, PASS, or REGISTER, are also omitted. Protocol
authentication commands not implemented by the client cannot enter history.
These omissions keep known credential forms out of later suggestions; they
are not a detector for every arbitrary secret a user might type into text.
Service-message omissions also include harmless messages to those services.

Enter with input focus, or Run, explicitly submits the prompt. An accepted command returns to
main chat editing unless it opens a panel such as Settings, Manual, or a list.
An invalid or refused command stays in Command for correction. Escape or
Cancel or Escape returns to the screen that opened Command, including the
Summary reader, without changing the chat draft or caret.
An empty prompt does nothing. /quit still explicitly exits the application.

Bracketed paste in Command inserts data. CR, LF, and Tab become spaces;
unsupported controls and input-limit violations are reported. Paste never
executes a command or activates a control. Review the text and use a fresh
Enter or Run to submit it. Chat paste remains literal and cannot execute
a local slash command.

Message commands /msg and /me retain their byte-budget warning, paced output,
and default-No multi-message confirmation. // sends a literal leading slash
through the same message path; it is not stored as command history. A
confirmation does not discard or replace the independent chat draft.
Channel Join and Query New actions open Command with /join or /pm prepared.

CONNECTION AND STARTUP COMMANDS

Connect directly without first creating a server profile or number:

    /connect irc.example.org
    /join #chat
    /saveconf

These connection and profile commands work in both vipirc interfaces. A new
destination uses verified TLS on port 6697 and a valid system login nickname,
or user if needed. An existing matching server retains its configured
transport, port, nickname, and authentication. An already active match is
selected instead of duplicated. New destinations do not inherit another
server's credentials or channels. No connection command saves implicitly.

    /connect [-tls|-plain] [-nick NICK] HOST [PORT]
    /connect              connect the selected saved/applied server
    /server HOST [PORT]   connect directly, like /connect HOST
    /server NUMBER        select a server without connecting it
    /server               open the selected server's messages and MOTD
    /server add HOST [PORT] [NICK]
                          add a disconnected, unsaved profile
    /server connect NUMBER
    /server disconnect NUMBER
    /disconnect [NUMBER] disconnect the selected or numbered server
    /server close NUMBER close a secondary server and its retained state

Options precede HOST. -tls or -ssl requests verified TLS; -plain explicitly
requests unencrypted IRC. A +PORT requests TLS; an ordinary numeric port
does not disable it. --tls, --plain, and --nick spellings are accepted too.
The default port for a new plaintext connection is 6667. Passwords are not
positional connection arguments. /server connect and disconnect do not
change selection. The permanent primary server is 0 in the full interface
and 1 in minimalist mode. /server close explicitly
discards that secondary session's views/drafts and cancels its transfers;
it removes the startup catalog entry while keeping the physical profile.

    /autoconnect [on|off]
    /autojoin [list|add #CHANNEL|remove #CHANNEL|clear]
    /autoauth [status|off|sasl USER file PATH|sasl USER gpg PATH]
    /save [input|output|all]
    /saveconf

Autoconnect changes the selected server's next-startup choice. Autojoin
stages the channel list for the next explicit /connect; it does not join or
part channels now. Save with /save or /saveconf to keep these choices for a
later process start. Automatic retries keep the interrupted connection's
settings. /autojoin shows the selected server,
registration/authentication state, running and pending lists, and membership.
For an active connection, /disconnect followed by /connect applies pending
settings. Use /join #channel to join a channel immediately after registration.
Autoauth stages SASL for the next explicit connection; verified TLS is required.
/autoauth status shows complete configured credential file paths locally,
without opening them. General /settings source reporting stays redacted.
In the full interface these inquiries open a scrollable reader with Refresh
and Back, preserving the originating screen and draft.
PATH is literal remaining text, including spaces, with no shell expansion.
The command does not open the credential file. Use Settings for explicitly
stored plaintext passwords; do not put passwords in commands. Disconnect
and reconnect explicitly to use changed connection/authentication settings.

/save saves the selected profile's effective settings, including staged
changes. /save input and /save output save the whole primary profile that
owns application preferences. /save all saves each healthy profile.
/saveconf saves application preferences and healthy profiles and remembers
the selected server for the next launch's /connect. Saving does not enable
autoconnect. Each file is replaced privately and atomically; a later failure
does not undo files already saved. Errors are reported and unreadable
profiles are not overwritten. Test mode never writes configuration.

/set autoconnect on|off is an alias for /autoconnect on|off. The /set
send_mode direct|review, /set composer_mode line|fullscreen, and /set
output_format compact|full preferences affect the minimalist interface and
belong to the primary profile.
/query NICK|NUMBER and /pm NICK|NUMBER open a query without sending a message.
/ls [servers|channels|queries|unread] opens a local list, with channels as
the default; it is not a network-wide IRC LIST request or shell command.
/list [MASK] requests the selected server's network channel directory and
opens the full-screen channel browser. It requires registration. MASK is the
only filter sent to IRC. --min-users N, --max-users N, --name TEXT and
--topic TEXT filter the received entries locally; --sort channel|users|topic,
--asc or --desc, and --limit N control presentation. Users descending is the
default. A display limit of 0 means no display limit within the bounded
8192-entry cache.

The channel browser has Channel, Users and Topic columns. Up/Down or j/k
selects rows. Left/Right or h/l changes the sort column; s reverses the sort.
Page Up/Page Down and g/G move through long lists. Enter joins the selected
channel; r repeats the current LIST with the same filters; / opens Command;
Escape returns. With the mouse enabled, clicking a column heading sorts it.

/list show opens the cached directory without another network request. Its
--sort, --asc/--desc and --limit options can change the cached presentation.
/list clear removes the cache. vipirc -i prints the same cached directory for
/list show. /ls or /cl lists channel views already retained by this client.

In both interfaces, /panel opens guided settings and /quickstart asks the
selected server's four connection essentials. Graphical /settings and F1
Settings keep the ordinary forms. /help [TEXT] opens the complete manual;
TEXT searches within it rather than printing separate topic help.
/help commands and /help ls find the command sections; /help all opens the
complete manual without an initial search. Connection/configuration command
results are retained in the server message view; errors also remain visible
in Command for correction.

SESSION SUMMARY

/summary opens a local snapshot of the whole running client in a separate
scrollable reader. It works while disconnected and groups entries by server.
It includes connection state and nickname, channel 0, joined and left
channel views, queries, unread and mention counts, outgoing queues, pending
startup commands, and file transfers with their current status. Totals omit
the copied mentions feed to avoid counting its source messages twice.
Mentions may also be unread messages; those two totals are not added together.

Opening or refreshing the summary does not switch conversations, mark them
read, send a network request, or replace a chat draft. It reports queue
counts without exposing queued message text, automatic-command text, or
credentials. It shows current state rather than interpreting chat content.

In the full interface, use Up/Down or k/j, Page Up/Page Down, and Home/End or
g/G to read. Press r or R, activate Refresh with the keyboard, or click
Refresh to take another snapshot. Escape or Back returns to the origin.
In vipirc -i, r refreshes the response reader. A failed refresh
retains the previous snapshot. Networking continues while the reader is open.
Slash opens Command from Summary; cancelling it returns to that snapshot.
Press ? to read help for the summary and its reader.

SETTINGS

Settings in the vipirc application panel, or /settings, opens an app-wide
home containing Interface, every server profile, and New server. Server rows
show their Auto-connect and saved/unsaved state. Select any profile to edit it
without switching the active chat. Edits remain staged until Apply or Save.
The server form scrolls through labelled fields. Up/Down or k/j selects
a field; Left/Right or h/l selects its footer action; Enter activates that
action. Home/End or g/G reaches the first/last field. Letters are ordinary
text while a field editor is open.

    Edit    Apply    Save    Back    Cancel

The editable groups contain:

    Connection fields: Server, Port, Transport, Nickname, Username, Real name,
      Auto-join channels, Auto-connect, Auto-authentication (none/sasl),
      Authentication user, Password file, GPG password file, Plaintext
      password, Server password file, GPG server password file, Plaintext
      server password, CA file.
    Server history: History lines.
    Interface home entry: app-wide User list, Mouse, Hints, Shortcut
    labels, Queue notices, Program messages, Persistent logging,
    Single-session mode, Command suggestions, and Default interface.
    Mentions: existing Watch term fields and Add watch term.
    Ignore: existing Ignore mask fields and Add ignore mask.

Hints are on by default. Settings > Interface > Hints changes optional key
reminders and field guidance; Apply changes every session, and Save persists
the choice in the primary configuration as [interface] hints=false or true.
Titles, source context, selected items, controls, errors, validation results,
and send/transfer safety confirmations remain visible with hints disabled.
Screen titles, content, actions, and status keep consistent positions; hints
use a quieter style in their reserved area.

Shortcut labels is on by default. Turning it off hides only the F1..F6
prefixes in the top bar; the keys continue to open their available screens.
Save retains [interface] shortcut_labels=false or true in the primary file.

Edit toggles a boolean checkbox, opens a two-option choice selector, or
opens a text/number field editor. Enter in an editor stages that field;
it does not Apply, Save, or send chat. Tab stages a valid value and advances
to the next field; Shift-Tab stages it and moves to the previous field.
Invalid values remain editable with their diagnostic. Editing an existing
watch term to
empty removes it; Add watch term creates another, within the usual bounds.
Ignore mask fields work the same way; an empty existing mask removes it.

Interface Apply updates these application preferences for all current
sessions and future server slots. Default interface selects the next fresh
launch and never changes the current frontend. Interface Save writes only the
primary configuration,
atomically and privately, before applying the global values. A failed or
blocked Save leaves every session unchanged. On startup, secondary profiles
use those primary interface choices even if they contain legacy local keys.
History lines remains per server.

Apply validates the staged configuration. It applies interface preferences,
mention terms, ignore masks, and auto-connect in memory, stays in Settings,
and resets the footer action to Edit. The applied values become the new
base for further edits. Apply does not write a configuration file.

Server, transport, identity, auto-join, authentication, and CA changes are
staged connection settings. The next explicit Connect while disconnected,
including /connect, adopts the applied values. Apply does not reconnect an
active session or change its current identity or transport. Use /nick, /join,
and /part for current-session changes. Save retains connection choices for
future launches; /save preserves applied pending choices while saving live
preferences. Trying applied connection settings requires neither Save nor a
restart.

Transport selects TLS (verified) or Plain IRC. It controls encryption of the
network connection, separately from password storage and SASL authentication.
The connection log says whether TLS is required with certificate verification,
or encryption is OFF because TLS is disabled. An unencrypted IRC connection
does not mean that a GPG-encrypted password file has become plaintext on disk.

Save validates and atomically writes this server's full configuration,
then applies live preferences and stays in Settings. Back returns to the
Settings home. The first Save of a new secondary server also creates its
isolated profile and startup
catalog entry. Other servers' configurations are not overwritten.
In --test-mode, Save is
disabled; Apply previews changes only in memory. Edit the file externally
and restart to make permanent test-mode configuration changes.

Cancel or Escape closes the entire Settings panel, including from a field
editor or choice popup. Unapplied changes are discarded without another
question. Applied preferences and pending connection values remain in memory;
chat drafts remain intact. Escape from Settings returns to vipirc, including
from a field editor or choice popup. Tab and Shift-Tab move among Settings
fields. Creating
or connecting a server from Settings keeps the active chat unchanged.

Changing Server to a case-insensitively different value clears inherited
Authentication, Authentication user, every account/server password source,
and Auto-join channels immediately in the staged form. Enter the intended
credentials and channels after choosing the new server. The active session
is untouched. File fields contain paths; Settings does not read or decrypt
their contents. Inline plaintext password fields are masked while viewing
and editing. They preserve spaces and require a private configuration file.

Bracketed paste is accepted only while a text/number field editor is open.
It inserts data without committing or closing the field. Tabs become spaces;
CR, LF, Escape, and unsupported control characters are rejected. Paste on
the Settings list or in a choice popup is ignored. Review pasted values,
then press Enter to stage the field. Warning and confirmation dialogs keep
their own cancel/acknowledgment behavior before global navigation.

TERMINAL SIGNALS

Ctrl-D is ignored, including when the draft is empty, except that it cancels
the F1 quit question without exiting. Pasted Ctrl-D cannot answer that
question.
To exit normally, run /quit in Command. Custom terminal signal
assignments still take precedence over ordinary key handling.

Unix terminal signal keys remain available. The usual Ctrl-C interrupt
exits without saving drafts; Ctrl-Z suspends the process, and the shell's
fg command resumes it. A suspended client cannot answer the server and may
time out.

RUNNING IN THE BACKGROUND

Use /background, or Background in the vipirc application screen, to keep
IRC connections, direct transfers, histories, and drafts running while
returning to the shell. The program restores the terminal and prints the
numbered resume command for this session, for example:

    vipirc --resume 1

vipirc --resume without an argument resumes the sole verified available
detached job. If several candidates exist, it shows their numbers and requires
a choice. vipirc --sessions lists local jobs without opening configuration or
requiring a terminal. --resume=1 is another accepted spelling. Numbers stay
stable while their jobs exist and may be reused after they exit. An explicit
absolute socket path remains accepted. If an older detached worker rejects the frontend-selecting attach request, vipirc retries the established attach protocol and uses that worker's existing frontend for that attachment; frontend switching becomes available after the worker itself is upgraded.

For unattended startup use vipirc --background --reconnect --config followed
by an absolute configuration path. The primary configuration's saved default
interface selects the frontend, or ncurses if unset. Add -i for minimalist
mode or -N for ncurses for this launch. No terminal or TERM setting is needed to start the
job; use --resume from a terminal later. A full-interface job initializes
its display using the attaching terminal's capabilities and size.
The worker creates its private resume endpoint before starting resolver
or credential helpers. The live IRC state is independent of the attached
frontend. `vipirc --resume` retains it; `vipirc -N --resume` selects ncurses
and `vipirc -i --resume` selects the minimalist interface. Switching frontends does not reconnect servers or replace
the worker: channels, queries, unread state, DCC state, drafts, and bounded
scrollback remain in the same process. A resume redraws retained history even
when no IRC line arrived while detached.

The live session itself is not saved to disk. A later reboot, explicit /quit,
or process termination ends it. Optional persistent logging saves transcript
records only; it does not make a dead session resumable. Startup autoconnect
profiles are a separate saved configuration feature.

The first Background action creates one detached worker and a private local
job endpoint. Normal foreground use has no extra helper process or local
socket. Repeated Background actions keep the same worker, number, and
endpoint. A
resumed terminal has a small foreground waiter for terminal signals and size
changes. Only one terminal can be attached at a time; an additional resume
attempt reports that the session is busy.

Resume can use a different terminal or SSH login session on the same machine
and Unix account. Terminal capabilities, locale, and geometry are read again.
The resume command requires its input, output, and error descriptors on the
same interactive terminal. It does not make a network listener or require
screen, tmux, or a new language runtime.

Ctrl-C in the resumed application exits normally. A terminal hangup detaches
the worker so its connections continue. Ctrl-Z restores the terminal and
stops the resumed foreground waiter; the worker continues servicing servers.
Use fg to redraw and resume interaction. This is different from stopping an
ordinary foreground process before its first Background action.

If a resolver or credential helper is still running on the first detach,
Background asks you to retry after it finishes. No half-detach occurs.
Normal exit removes the private endpoint. The directory and socket are
owner-only. Discovery checks at most 64 fixed slots with one 1500 ms deadline
for all probes. It removes only verified stale entries whose lifetime lease
is no longer held, without PID lookup or process signalling. Unresponsive
live jobs remain listed as unverified and prevent automatic selection by
bare --resume. With [session] single_session=true, creation of a second
background job in the same vipirc namespace is refused, so bare --resume stays
unambiguous while that setting is in use. This does not limit the multiple IRC
servers connected inside one job. Numbered attachment checks the queried job's
incarnation before accepting terminal descriptors, so a reused number cannot
redirect it during handoff. Another process under the same account is within
the trust boundary.
Explicit Background also works with offline simulation and creates
only this local endpoint, without enabling IRC or DCC network activity.

SERVERS AND UNREAD ACTIVITY

Up to eight server sessions share this process and terminal. Each has
independent configuration, credentials, nicknames, channels, queries,
mentions, users, retained history, drafts, and cursor/scroll positions.
Background connections keep receiving messages and answering protocol
traffic through the same event loop.

Open Servers with F2, or run /servers in Command.
Up/Down or k/j selects a server row. Left/Right or h/l chooses its action
in the row directly beneath the heading and Enter executes it. Open is
selected initially and opens that server's message view (channel 0), showing
its MOTD and server messages. Horizontal arrows never open another category.

The selected server and action are highlighted together. Changing the row
preserves the action; Up/Down stops at the first/last row. Available actions:

    Open    New    Connect    Disconnect    Close    Away    Back

Enter executes the action for that row. Open shows the server's messages
directly; F3 or /channels opens its channel list. Chat drafts and carets
are preserved. Connect and Disconnect act on the
selected server.
Away toggles the selected registered server between the default away message
Away and return from away; the row reflects the server's acknowledgment.
New, also available as n in the list, opens the new server form. Back or
Escape returns to chat. Home/End or g/G selects the first/last row while
preserving the chosen action. A mouse click on a server also opens its
message view; clicks on the action row apply to the selected item.

The primary server is entry 0 and cannot be closed. Disconnect keeps its
views, history, and drafts; accepted direct file transfers continue. A
secondary Close always asks first and defaults to no. Confirming discards
that server's drafts/history, cancels its offers/transfers, and removes its
saved startup catalog reference while keeping the physical profile file.
Closing the current secondary returns to the primary main screen. In test
mode, Close affects only runtime state and never changes saved files.

New server form

Basic fields are Server, Port, Transport, Nickname, Auto-join channels,
and Auto-connect. Its footer is:

    Edit    Add    Connect    Advanced    Cancel

Use Edit to change the selected field. Advanced expands the form to all
startup connection fields, including Username, Real name, Auto-authentication,
Authentication user, all three account/server password-source choices, and
CA file.
This allows credentials to be configured before a first connection. The
Advanced button becomes Basic when expanded. Enter in a field only stages
its value; Escape cancels the whole form. Field paste follows Settings rules.

Fresh servers default to verified TLS on port 6697, a valid system login
nickname/username or fallback, and no authentication, credential-file paths,
CA override, channels, watch strings, or ignore masks. Only interface
preferences copy from the primary profile. Auto-connect defaults to false.

Add validates and creates a disconnected session, even if Auto-connect is
checked. Connect validates, creates, and connects immediately. Both switch
to the new server's main screen. Neither writes configuration. Use /save or
Settings > Save explicitly to retain this profile across launches.

Activity indicators

Server, channel, and query rows start with new N !M: unread activity and
unread mentions. The ! marker is explained in the list header. Counts above
999 display as 999+ while the internal counters remain exact. The main
unread-view count includes background servers.

Showing a main conversation clears only that source view's counts. A list
covering the current conversation does not mark arriving text read. Server
totals aggregate source server/channel/query views and exclude the copied
Mentions feed and Manual, avoiding duplicated counts. Opening Mentions
marks its feed read independently and does not clear source conversation
counts. Outgoing local echoes do not add unread activity.

F5 and /unread open a workspace-wide Mentions/unread browser. Mentions
appear first, followed by Unread conversations, each beneath nonselectable
group and server headings. Mention entries show the complete wrapped line
with its original timestamp. Unread entries identify their Server, Channel,
or Query source.
M in the header counts retained mention lines; U counts unread source
conversations. Mention copies and Help never duplicate unread source counts.

The action row beneath the title offers Open, Clear mentions, and Back.
Up/Down or k/j selects an entry; Left/Right or h/l selects its action, and
Enter executes it. Open is selected initially. A mouse click on an entry
also opens its source. A closed query can be reopened locally using its
recorded nickname; this does not send a message or restore discarded query
history. Closed channel views are not joined automatically, and an unavailable
server is reported instead of opening a replacement. Source identities are
tracked independently of the visible row positions and displayed text.

Clear mentions, or /mentions clear, removes the retained mention copies
across all servers. Conversation histories, unread source counts, drafts,
and messages waiting to be sent remain intact. New mentions can arrive
after clearing. Home/End or g/G selects the first/last entry. Page Up/Page
Down scrolls a long selected mention before moving to adjacent entries.
Back or Escape returns to main chat. Channel/query list numbering is
unchanged.
Bare /mentions opens the current server's separate mention feed.

Every server has its own server/MOTD entry 0, channel list, query list,
mentions feed, and rosters. Channel and query headers identify their server.
The server view contains registration, MOTD, connection, and error messages.
Each channel or private conversation has a separate view. The mentions view
collects matching received lines with their original displayed timestamps,

F5 opens the combined Mentions/unread browser. /users and Settings > Interface

CHANNEL CHOOSER AND CLOSING CONVERSATIONS

Use F3, the Channels header destination, or /channels.
Entry 0 in Channels is always the server's MOTD view. Other entries are that
server's channel views, including left channels whose history is retained.

Up/Down or k/j selects a channel row. Left/Right or h/l chooses its action
beneath the heading and Enter executes it; Open is selected initially. Both
selections
are highlighted together, and changing the row preserves the action.
Horizontal arrows stay within this list. Available actions:

    Open    Join    Part    Close    Back

Up/Down stops at the first/last row. Join opens the separate Command prompt
with /join prepared, preserving chat drafts and caret positions. Part leaves
the channel and keeps history; Close removes
the view. Back or Escape returns to main chat editing.

draft asks first, defaulting to No. The server entry cannot be parted or

/close [NAME|CHANNELNUMBER] also closes a channel or query; without an
argument
it closes the current conversation. Server and mentions views cannot be
removed. Channel numbers can change after closing a channel; use the current
